no_fit_reason: This process is fundamentally a hands-on physical task. While forklift maintenance has information components (logs, manuals, inventory), the core pain points are about physical inspection and repair work, scheduling coordination across warehouse operations, and parts logistics—not about processing, extracting, classifying, or generating information. AI cannot perform physical inspection of equipment, hands-on repair, or directly solve inventory supply chain delays. Scheduling optimization and inventory management are tangential to the core maintenance work itself, and would require domain-specific tools beyond what general-purpose AI assistants or classifiers address. This process is not a good candidate for AI.

process: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that reads manager narrative comments and prior review scores, then generates a structured draft performance summary (strengths, development areas, recommended rating justification) for the manager to edit and refine before submission.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the wide variation in write-up quality and tone by offering a consistent, structured template and language suggestions. Managers retain full control and can edit the draft, which is essential for a sensitive personnel decision.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardizes narrative structure and tone across reviews, reducing inconsistency while preserving manager judgment.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Performance review consistency and fairness are core HR governance priorities in a large organization.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Manager comments and prior scores are well-structured, existing HR system data.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: LLM-based summarization and structuring is straightforward; no custom model needed.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Managers must accept a new pre-draft step, but the assistant is advisory only, so resistance should be low.
criteria_rationale.off_the_sheet: LLM-based writing assistants for HR are becoming mature, though some custom tuning to company tone/policies is typical.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: High risk because this use case directly supports performance evaluation and may influence promotion, termination, or pay decisions; it profiles employee behavior and performance.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive personal data (performance evaluations, employment history) of identified individuals.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags draft reviews as requiring calibration discussion (e.g., outlier ratings, significant tone shifts, or conflicts with peer comparisons), versus routine reviews that can be approved without further calibration prep.
use_cases.justification: This targets the time-consuming calibration-meeting preparation by pre-filtering which reviews actually need discussion, letting HR schedule and prepare only those sessions with focused agendas.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces calibration-meeting churn by identifying genuine outliers, with modest consistency gains.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves HR process efficiency, a secondary operational priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Prior scores and peer comparisons are available but require linking multiple HR systems; some manual data prep is typical.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires custom rule-based or supervised learning logic to detect meaningful outliers and inconsistencies; not off-the-shelf.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR teams must trust the flagging criteria, but the classifier is advisory; adoption risk is moderate.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No commodity tool exists for this specific calibration triage; custom build is required.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: High risk because it directly influences which employee performance reviews receive scrutiny and calibration, affecting fairness and consistency of personnel decisions.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive performance and personal data of identified employees, including peer comparisons.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An AI tool that extracts and summarizes key terms (coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, renewal dates, premium costs) from current policy documents and broker quotes, structuring them into comparable fields.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the manual broker quote comparison pain point by automatically pulling structured data from multiple policy documents, eliminating the need for line-by-line manual review and spreadsheet entry.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistently extracts key terms from complex policy PDFs, reducing transcription errors and missed clauses.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control and procurement efficiency, core to supply chain management.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Policy documents and quotes are structured PDFs; extraction is reliable for standardized fields.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Document extraction from PDFs is a mature, well-established pattern with off-the-shelf tools.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Finance team still reviews the output and makes final decisions; tool is a time-saver, not a workflow overhaul.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document-extraction tools handle insurance policy PDFs routinely.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal procurement document processing with no profiling of individuals or external parties.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes company policy and broker data; no sensitive personal data involved.

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags broker quotes as low-risk (clear coverage improvements, lower cost), medium-risk (trade-offs to review), or high-risk (coverage gaps, missing riders) based on comparison to current policy and claims history.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the rushed decision-making near renewal deadline by prioritizing which quotes deserve deep legal/insurance expert review, reducing the number of quotes requiring specialist time and accelerating the decision cycle.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces wasted expert time on routine comparisons, but still requires human judgment on nuanced trade-offs.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Shortens renewal cycle and reduces deadline pressure, supporting operational efficiency and risk management priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Requires structured claims history and consistent policy field data; quality depends on extraction step working well.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires custom training on internal claims history and policy structures; medium build effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Changes workflow by routing quotes to experts based on risk flag; moderate adoption effort to integrate into renewal process.
criteria_rationale.off_the_sheet: No off-the-shelf tool tailors insurance quote triage to this company's specific claims history and priorities.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal procurement triage with no external profiling or regulated decision-making.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes company claims history and policy data; no sensitive personal data exposed externally.

use_cases.description: A classifier that evaluates incoming return requests against eligibility criteria (purchase date, return window, product condition) and flags them as auto-approvable, needs-review, or deny, with reasoning for the agent.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the inconsistent return decisions across agents and the time spent manually checking multiple systems to verify eligibility. By applying the policy consistently to every request, it removes subjectivity and reduces the agent's lookup work to data validation.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies return policy consistently to every request, eliminating agent-to-agent variation in eligibility decisions.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports operational consistency and customer satisfaction, both key to B2B distribution retention.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Order history, return policy rules, and purchase dates are structured and readily available; product condition data depends on photo quality.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on structured fields (date ranges, policy rules) plus optional image review is a mature pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents still issue the final approval and communicate with customers, so the workflow change is minimal.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Return-eligibility classifiers are common in e-commerce and B2B support platforms.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal classification of return requests with no profiling or behavior-based decisions; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Touches customer order and product data, which is indirectly personal but not sensitive.

use_cases.description: A chat assistant that retrieves order and return-policy information in real time, presents it to the agent in a structured summary, and suggests the eligibility outcome, without making the final decision.
use_cases.justification: This targets the high volume of repetitive return-eligibility questions and the time agents spend checking multiple systems. By automating information retrieval and presentation, it reduces lookup time and surfaces the data the agent needs to make a fast, consistent decision.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces agent search time and aggregates data, but does not change the quality of the final decision.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports high-volume request handling and consistency, both critical to customer-service SLAs.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Order history and policy rules are well-structured and readily available in existing systems.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Data retrieval and summarization for an agent tool is straightforward; no custom model required.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents are already accustomed to reference tools; this is a natural evolution.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Retrieval-based assistant frameworks and chatbot platforms already handle this pattern.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Agent-facing information retrieval with no autonomous decision-making; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses the same indirectly personal order and policy data as the classifier.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that automatically extracts and structures transaction data from bank statements (dates, amounts, descriptions, reference numbers) and matches them against general ledger entries in real-time, flagging unmatched or discrepant items for manual review.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the core pain point: manual matching of thousands of transactions is the most time-consuming and error-prone part of reconciliation. Automated extraction and fuzzy matching of GL transactions to bank statement lines will eliminate routine manual lookups and catch potential discrepancies early, allowing controllers to focus on resolution of genuine exceptions rather than mechanical matching.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies consistent, rule-based matching across all transactions; eliminates human manual-review fatigue errors and catches systematic mismatches that tired reviewers miss under deadline pressure.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports compliance and cost control by reducing month-end close time and risk of undetected errors; aligns with finance process efficiency.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Bank statements and GL data are structured, complete, and reliable; prior reconciliation workpapers provide training examples and historical patterns.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: OCR for bank statements plus deterministic fuzzy matching on amounts, dates, and reference fields is a proven pattern; some custom GL integration may be needed.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Controllers still review flagged discrepancies and approve the final reconciliation; the tool removes tedious manual matching, so adoption should be smooth.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several mature reconciliation-automation tools (e.g., BlackLine, Anacomp) already offer bank-GL matching as a core module.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal financial reconciliation with no profiling or decision-making on employees or customers; minimal regulatory risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes bank and GL transaction data; indirectly personal in that GL may contain employee reimbursement or payroll entries, but not sensitive personal data.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that searches historical reconciliation workpapers and GL documentation to retrieve prior explanations, resolutions, and posting details for recurring discrepancies (e.g., timing differences, in-transit items, intercompany transactions). The assistant presents the most likely resolution context to speed up manual investigation of flagged items.
use_cases.justification: This targets the second-order pain point: once discrepancies are identified, controllers must manually trace each one through prior workpapers and GL notes, a process that repeats for similar issues month-to-month. An assistant that retrieves historical context will cut investigation time for recurring or similar discrepancies, allowing faster root-cause isolation and posting decisions under deadline pressure.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Speeds consistency by retrieving prior resolutions; reduces risk of re-solving the same discrepancy differently month-to-month, though the controller still decides.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces close-timeline pressure and supports efficient month-end process, a secondary operational priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Historical workpapers exist but are partly unstructured (PDF notes, scanned documents, email threads); some manual indexing or OCR will be needed for reliable retrieval.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Semantic search or RAG over historical documents is a mature capability; straightforward integration with existing document storage.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Zero workflow disruption; the tool merely surfaces information the controller already needs, so adoption is minimal.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: General-purpose document search and retrieval tools (e.g., enterprise search, RAG platforms) are commodities; no special build required.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal information retrieval from prior reconciliation records; no profiling or automated decision-making on employees or external parties.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses the same reconciliation and GL data as the extraction use case; indirectly personal but not sensitive.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that reads an approved post from the content calendar and automatically formats and populates it into each social platform's scheduler (LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Facebook) with correct dimensions, hashtags, and platform-specific metadata.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of manually copying approved content into each platform's scheduler. The assistant retrieves the approved post and posting guidelines, formats it for each platform's requirements, and auto-fills the scheduler fields, eliminating repetitive manual copy-paste and reformatting work.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Eliminates manual formatting errors and ensures consistent application of platform guidelines across all channels.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves marketing efficiency but is a tactical back-office task, not a revenue or strategic driver.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Content calendar, creative assets, and platform guidelines are structured and readily available today.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: API integration with schedulers and template-based formatting is a well-established pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Marketers still control what gets posted; the tool only automates the mechanical scheduling step.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several social media management platforms (Hootsuite, Buffer, Sprout Social) offer similar automation.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal content scheduling with no profiling of employees or regulated decision-making is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data is processed; only internal content and platform-agnostic posting metadata.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads approval sign-offs and content metadata and auto-assigns each post to one of three states: Ready to Schedule, Awaiting Stakeholder Approval, or Published, with a notification trigger to the owner when approval is received or missing.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the pain point of coordinating approval across multiple stakeholders and tracking pending versus published posts. The classifier scans sign-offs and flags posts stuck in approval, alerting owners to follow up without manual status-checking.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces manual status-checking and improves visibility into approval bottlenecks.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves workflow efficiency and reduces approval delays, a tactical priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approval sign-offs and post metadata are structured and available in the content calendar system.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification based on approval status and metadata fields is straightforward.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Marketers adjust to receiving automated alerts instead of manual status checks; a minor workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Most content calendar and project-management platforms offer basic approval workflows; enhanced classification can be added via API.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal workflow routing with no profiling of employee performance or behavior is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Indirectly touches employee names and approval timestamps but does not profile or evaluate them.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads incoming IT incident tickets and auto-assigns severity level (critical, high, medium, low) based on ticket description, system logs, and historical incident patterns.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the inconsistent severity categorization pain point, applying a consistent logic to every ticket submission and ensuring that on-call engineers see the correct priority immediately, reducing time spent on severity assessment.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies severity rules consistently, reducing the variance introduced by manual categorization and catching high-severity tickets that might otherwise be missed.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports operational efficiency and incident response time, a core priority for IT support SLAs.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket descriptions, system logs, and historical incident data are well-structured and readily available in most ticketing systems.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on structured text and categorical fields is a standard ML pattern; most ticketing systems have APIs for integration.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Engineers can override the auto-assigned severity, so this is a time-saving aid rather than a constraint on their workflow.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several IT service management platforms (Jira Service Management, ServiceNow) have built-in or partner ML-based severity classification.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal IT operations triage with no profiling or decision-making about individuals.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: May touch employee identifiers in logs or on-call data, but only in a process-flow context, not as a subject of profiling.

use_cases.description: An extraction tool that parses ticket descriptions and system logs to identify and link duplicate or related incidents for the same underlying issue, surfacing them to the engineer before assignment.
use_cases.justification: This targets the duplicate-ticket detection pain point, reducing wasted effort by identifying when multiple tickets are for the same incident and consolidating them early, so the on-call engineer handles one unified case instead of multiple fragmented ones.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Deduplication reduces redundant investigation and rework, though a human must still validate the linkage.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves resolution efficiency and reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR), a core IT support KPI.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket descriptions and logs are available, but duplication often involves semantic matching across varied descriptions, which requires some data normalization.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires semantic similarity matching (embedding-based or fuzzy matching) across ticket descriptions and log correlation; moderate custom development.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Presents recommendations to engineers, who make the merge decision, so adoption friction is low.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Deduplication is not a standard out-of-box feature in most ticketing systems; would require custom ML or a third-party specialized tool.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal incident deduplication with no profiling or decision-making about individuals.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes ticket content and logs that may reference employee names or identifiers in an indirect, operational context.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that recommends the correct on-call owner for each ticket based on the ticket category, severity, and on-call rotation schedule, then retrieves their current status and availability.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the pain point of on-call engineers spending time figuring out ticket ownership, by automating the lookup and recommendation logic so they know immediately who owns the ticket and whether that person is available.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies deterministic routing rules correctly every time; minor quality gain because the logic is already relatively well-defined.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves operational efficiency and reduces manual overhead, but is a secondary priority compared to incident resolution speed.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: On-call schedules, ticket categories, and severity levels are structured and reliable; this is high-confidence data.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: A simple lookup and rule-based recommendation engine, trivial to build and integrate with standard ticketing APIs.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Presents a suggestion that engineers can ignore or override, so it is non-disruptive.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Most modern ticketing and on-call management tools (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira Service Management) already have rule-based routing.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Automated routing recommendation based on role and schedule, with no profiling or behavioral assessment.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses on-call engineer names and schedule data, which is indirectly personal in an organizational context.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads sales transaction data and applies the commission plan rules automatically, extracting and calculating the correct commission for each transaction, including territory and product-line exceptions.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the error-prone manual spreadsheet calculations and the complexity of region/product-line exceptions. By consistently applying the rules to every transaction, it eliminates calculation disputes and reduces the time spent on manual formula entry and verification.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies complex commission rules consistently to every transaction, eliminating manual formula errors and rep disputes over calculations.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control and revenue retention by reducing rep dissatisfaction and payroll errors.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Sales transaction data, rep territory assignments, and commission rules are all structured and readily available in the ERP/CRM system.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires custom rule engine to encode territorial and product-line exceptions, plus integration with transaction data sources.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Reps may initially distrust automated calculations, but clear rule transparency and audit trails reduce resistance.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No commodity tool exists that handles this company's specific, multi-dimensional exception rules.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal commission calculation with no profiling or decision-making about employees—purely computational.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Touches rep earnings data (indirectly personal) but no sensitive categories.

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags calculated commission records for manual review based on anomaly detection: outliers, threshold breaches, or rule conflicts that the extraction step flagged as uncertain.
use_cases.justification: This targets the tight payroll deadline by routing only the edge cases that need human review, so operations staff can prioritize and avoid last-minute corrections. It also provides a safety check before final payroll submission.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces manual review effort on routine records while catching anomalies that need human judgment before payroll is locked.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports operational efficiency and reduces payroll deadline pressure, a secondary priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Builds on structured commission data already calculated and validated by the extraction use case.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: A simple anomaly detection classifier on numeric fields; standard statistical methods suffice.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: No change to ops staff workflow—just a triage layer that filters their review queue.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Anomaly detection on numeric data is a mature, off-the-shelf capability.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal anomaly flagging, no autonomous decisions made without human review.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses the same indirectly personal rep earnings data as the extraction step.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that automatically extracts key information (employee identity, right-to-work status, tax details, employment contract terms) from identity documents, right-to-work forms, tax forms, and contracts, and structures them for compliance review.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the manual document review bottleneck by automating extraction from the multiple disconnected sources, reducing the time HR spends on data entry and initial validation. It improves consistency in capturing all required fields and reduces the risk of missing or misread information.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistent extraction of identity and tax data reduces transcription errors and ensures no field is missed, improving accuracy over manual review.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports on-time system access and compliance, which are core HR operational priorities in a regulated distribution business.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Documents are submitted by new hires but are structured (contracts, forms, ID) with clear expected fields; overall good data quality.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Multi-document OCR and field extraction is a mature capability but requires some customization per document type (ID, tax forms, contracts).
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR still reviews the extracted data before approval, so workflow changes are minimal; adoption is straightforward.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several enterprise HR-focused document AI platforms (e.g., Workable, BambooHR integrations, or dedicated onboarding AI tools) offer this out of the box.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Minimal risk: internal HR processing of onboarding documents with no algorithmic decision-making on the new hire, only data extraction.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Sensitive: processes identity documents, right-to-work documents, and tax forms, which contain personal and sometimes sensitive data (e.g., passport numbers, national ID).

use_cases.description: A classifier that takes the extracted onboarding data and automatically checks it against the HR compliance checklist, flagging documents as 'complete', 'missing documents', or 'needs manual review', to route cases appropriately.
use_cases.justification: This targets the delay in system access caused by missing documents and manual checklist-matching. By automatically comparing extracted data against the compliance checklist, it accelerates the identification of gaps and routes complete packages directly to provisioning, while flagging exceptions for HR attention.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies the checklist consistently and exhaustively to every new hire, eliminating the missed-document problem that occurs with manual review.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces delays in system access, a key pain point impacting new hire experience and operational readiness.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Operates on the structured extracted data from the first use case plus the static compliance checklist, both high quality.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: A simple rule-based or ML classifier matching extracted fields against a checklist; straightforward to build.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR still makes final decisions on incomplete packages; this only automates the matching step, so minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Rule-based compliance checklist matching is a standard capability in HR platforms and onboarding tools.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Minimal risk: applies a fixed compliance checklist with no discretionary algorithmic decision-making on the new hire.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Sensitive: reviews and classifies the same sensitive personal data extracted in the first use case.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that processes inspection checklists and site photos to automatically extract structured hazard data, severity level, location, and equipment involved—converting free-text inspector notes into consistent, queryable fields.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the inconsistent free-text notes problem by enforcing consistent data capture at the point of inspection. Structured extraction enables reliable cross-referencing of recurring hazards across sites without manual search through past reports.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardized extraction ensures all hazards are recorded consistently and completely, reducing missed details compared to variable manual notes.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports safety compliance and risk management, a top priority in regulated B2B distribution operations.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Inspection checklists and site photos are captured routinely; incident history is available but may need normalization.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: OCR plus structured field extraction from images and forms is a well-proven pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Inspectors continue filling out checklists and taking photos; the AI augments rather than replaces their workflow.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document extraction and form-reading tools exist for this use case.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal safety inspection data processing with no profiling of individuals is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Touches site location and incident data; employee inspector names may appear but are indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: A classifier that tags extracted hazards as recurring (matched against historical incidents) or novel, and flags corrective actions as overdue based on date and assigned owner.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the manual cross-referencing burden by automatically identifying patterns in hazard data once it is structured. It also closes the gap in tracking corrective action completion by surfacing overdue items without human review of logs.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Automated pattern matching and due-date flagging catch recurring hazards and overdue actions consistently, eliminating oversight.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Enables proactive hazard management and accountability for corrective action closure, both critical for safety compliance and operational risk reduction.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Structured hazard data from extraction is clean; corrective action logs exist but may have incomplete or non-standard date and owner fields.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification and rule-based matching on structured fields is straightforward once extraction is in place.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Safety managers receive automated alerts; no change to inspection or action-logging workflows.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Pattern matching and task-status classification are commodity ML capabilities, though may require customization to site-specific hazard taxonomy.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal hazard tracking and task triage with no decisions about individuals is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses incident and action data with minimal personal data exposure.
